# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤚]

I see a purple light, display reading 0, and three wires: 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Mute’s earlier 🤚 has no agreed meaning yet, so I cannot safely treat it as an instruction. I will give both others the full visible state, ask Blind to report every tactile control, and ask Mute to translate the relevant manual instruction into a simple agreed gesture code for wire choice or non-wire action.

``` 
speak(text="Visible state: display reads 0; light is purple; wires are 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Blind: describe every part you can feel, but do not act. Mute: consult the manual for this exact state. Reply by gesture using 👍 for wire 1, 👎 for wire 2, 👌 for wire 3, or ✋ if the manual says do not cut a wire; then add any further gestures needed for the required action.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The light has changed from purple to yellow while the display remains 0 and the same three wires remain visible. Under the code I proposed, Mute’s ✋ means the manual does not call for cutting a wire. We still need identify the reachable control and obtain an unambiguous manual instruction for it. I will establish a compact gesture vocabulary that Blind can use to describe what they feel and Mute can use to specify the required action.

```text
speak(text="Update: light is now yellow; display still 0; wires unchanged. Mute's ✋ means do not cut any wire. Blind, do not act. Report tactile controls by gestures: 🖐=button, ✊=switch, 🤏=dial/knob, 🤚=lever/handle, 👊=socket/slot, 🙌=other; repeat the class gesture once per item, then gesture its position: ☝=left, 👌=middle, 👉=right, 👆=top, 👇=bottom. Mute: once Blind's control report is known, send the manual's required action using 🖐=press button, ✊=toggle switch, 🤏=turn dial, 🤚=move lever, 👊=use socket, and position gestures as above. Use 👍/👎/👌 only if a wire cut is later required.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The light is now orange; the display and wire colours remain unchanged. Mute again sent ✋, consistently indicating either “do not cut” or “wait,” so no wire should be touched. Blind has not provided a visible tactile report, so there is still no safe basis for an action. I will explicitly ask Mute whether ✋ means wait and request the manual’s condition/action in a gesture encoding, while asking Blind again for a concise tactile inventory.

```text
speak(text="No action yet. The light has progressed purple, yellow, orange; display remains 0; wires remain green, blue, yellow. Mute: I interpret repeated ✋ as WAIT/DO NOT ACT. If that is correct, send 👍. If it instead means a specific non-wire control action, send 👎 followed by the action code: 🖐 press, ✊ toggle, 🤏 turn, 🤚 move; then its position ☝ left, 👌 middle, 👉 right, 👆 top, or 👇 bottom. Blind: please now gesture your tactile inventory using the code I gave; do not operate anything.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]

Mute confirmed that ✋ means wait/do not act. Their additional 👌 may be the wire-3 symbol from our earlier convention, but it is ambiguous whether it is a future instruction or an instruction to cut now. Because an ambiguous action is fatal, Blind must continue waiting until Mute explicitly confirms both “cut wire 3” and “now,” ideally after stating the manual condition that makes it safe. The light has returned to purple, suggesting a cycle, while display and wires remain unchanged.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Do not touch any wire or control. Mute confirmed that ✋ means wait/do not act. We do not yet have an unambiguous execute-now instruction.")

speak(to="mute", text="I received 👍 confirming ✋ means WAIT. I also received 👌. Did 👌 mean CUT WIRE 3 NOW, or only that wire 3 will matter later? Do not rely on it yet. If Blind should cut wire 3 immediately, send 👍 then 👌 then 👍. If Blind must continue waiting, send ✋ only. If another action is required, send its action/position code after 👎.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The light is yellow again, confirming a repeating purple–yellow–orange cycle. Mute has sent ✋ again, which they explicitly confirmed means wait/do not act. The earlier 👌 therefore cannot safely be treated as an immediate cut command, particularly since Mute has returned to wait. Blind must not touch anything.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="WAIT. Do not cut a wire or operate any control. Mute again signals ✋, confirmed as wait/do not act. Current visible state: yellow light, display 0, wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow.")

speak(to="mute", text="I relayed your ✋ as WAIT. When an action is required, please send a clear execute sequence in one message: 👍 then the action symbol, then 👍. For wires: 🖐=wire 1 green, ✊=wire 2 blue, 👌=wire 3 yellow. For no action, send ✋.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The visible state is orange with display 0 and unchanged wires. Mute continues to indicate wait. However, my earlier redefinition of the wire symbols was inconsistent with the original convention and could cause confusion; I need correct it. No action should occur absent an explicit manual-derived command and Blind’s tactile information.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="WAIT; do not touch the bomb. Current state remains display 0, orange light, wires 1 green / 2 blue / 3 yellow. Ignore any prior wire-symbol mapping unless Mute gives you a direct instruction.")

speak(to="mute", text="I see ✋ again and am treating it as WAIT. Important correction: do not use my improvised wire code. To instruct Blind safely, say the wire number aloud in words (for example, 'cut wire three') or use your own agreed gesture explanation first. Please send an explicit action only when the manual says it is safe.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The light is purple again, with display 0 and unchanged wires. Mute’s repeated ✋ is safely understood only as “do not cut a wire”; it does not establish whether Blind should operate some non-wire control. Since Blind can report tactile details to Mute by speech, Mute should relay the manual’s complete instruction to me in a clear, pre-agreed gesture sequence, which I can then state aloud to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Do not cut any wire. Current visible state: purple light, display 0, wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Tell Mute aloud every control you can feel and whether there is any button, switch, dial, lever, or timer; do not operate it.")

speak(to="mute", text="I understand ✋ as DO NOT CUT. For this exact purple/0/green-blue-yellow state, does the manual require a non-wire action? If no action at all, send ✋ then 👍. If an action is required, send 👎 then one action sign: 🖐=press, ✊=toggle, 🤏=turn, 🤚=move; then position: ☝=left, 👌=middle, 👉=right, 👆=top, 👇=bottom. For a wire cut, use 👍=wire 1, 👎=wire 2, 👌=wire 3, preceded by 🖐 to mean CUT. I will relay only a complete instruction.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👍]

Mute’s sequence ✋ 👍 matches the clarification I requested for “no action at all.” Therefore Blind should continue to wait. The changing light is cycling yellow now, while display 0 and the wire arrangement remain unchanged; there is no new safe action condition.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="WAIT. Mute has confirmed that the manual requires no action in this state. Do not cut wires or operate any control. Visible state: yellow light, display 0, wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow.")

speak(to="mute", text="Understood: ✋ 👍 means no action. I will keep Blind waiting. Please signal immediately if the manual condition changes or if display/light state calls for an action.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👌]

Mute’s gesture sequence 🖐 👌 matches the wire-action code: cut wire 3. Wire 3 is yellow. The current light is orange and display remains 0; this is the first explicit action instruction rather than a wait signal.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Act now: cut wire 3, the yellow wire. Do not touch wires 1 or 2.")
```
